_readme: TYPES (adapters) — adding a new source never requires new code, only a new entry here:
'rss'         = a confirmed, working RSS/Atom feed. Each entry's title+summary is run through
label-anchored extraction (automation/extract.py). Auto-publishes ONLY if every
required field is confidently extracted, validated, and its URLs match officialDomains.
'manual_page' = a public notices page with no feed. The bot link-diffs it (new (text, href) pairs since
last check). For each new link it then fetches THAT single linked page (still respecting
robots.txt) and runs the same label-anchored extraction on it. If the linked page is a PDF,
extraction is NOT attempted (unreliable) and the item always goes to needs_review.
'json_api'    = a genuine official JSON API with a documented field mapping (see the disabled template
entry below). None of the sources researched for this project have a confirmed official
JSON API for recruitment notices — this type exists for when/if one appears.
'unsuitable_for_live_monitoring' / 'needs_verification' = as before: known, listed for transparency, not checked.
'officialDomains' is a hard allow-list: even a perfectly-extracted listing is rejected to needs_review if its
notification/apply URL isn't on this list for that source. This stops a compromised/mirrored/lookalike page
from ever reaching auto-publish.
'org' and 'category' are FIXED per source (we know which body's own site we're watching — that's not a guess).
Only the per-notice fields (title, vacancies, qualification, age, dates) are extracted from fetched text, and
ONLY those that are extracted with high confidence and pass validation lead to auto-publish; anything else
goes to needs_review. See AUTOMATION-GUIDE.md's source table for which of the sources below realistically
clear that bar today — for most, official notifications are PDFs, which this system does not attempt to
parse (unreliable), so expect most real detections to land in needs_review, not auto-publish. That is a
structural limitation of these sources, not a gap left to be filled in later.
'enabled': false means the checker skips it. Flip to true only after YOU have opened the URL and are
comfortable with this project's approach for that specific site (robots.txt-respecting, low-frequency,
read-only, no login/CAPTCHA bypass).

sources.name: Staff Selection Commission — notices
sources.notes: No public RSS/API. SSC notifications are published as PDFs — automatic field extraction will rarely succeed; expect items to land in needs_review. Verify the exact 'Notices' page URL before enabling.

sources.name: Railway Recruitment Boards — apply portal
sources.notes: Each regional RRB (e.g. RRB Mumbai, RRB Chennai) publishes separately with its own domain — duplicate this entry per region you want tracked, with that region's real domain in officialDomains. Notifications are typically PDFs.

sources.name: Institute of Banking Personnel Selection
sources.notes: No official feed. Notifications are typically PDFs. Individual public-sector banks publish separately.

sources.name: Union Public Service Commission — active notices
sources.notes: No confirmed official feed. Notifications are typically PDFs.

sources.name: CTET (Central Teacher Eligibility Test)
sources.notes: No official feed. State TET boards must be added individually — they vary by state.

sources.name: [Add your state's Public Service Commission]
sources.notes: Template — duplicate per state. There is no single 'State Government' source.

sources.name: Employment News / Rozgar Samachar (weekly e-paper)
sources.notes: Weekly PDF e-paper. Always PDF — extraction will not be attempted; every detection lands in needs_review by design. Check at most weekly.

sources.name: Press Information Bureau — press releases
sources.notes: Could not confirm a current, stable RSS URL in this project. If you verify one, change type to 'rss' and fill in url. Covers general press releases, not a purpose-built recruitment feed — expect very few relevant items even if enabled.

sources.name: data.gov.in — Open Government Data Platform (vacancy-related datasets)
sources.notes: Real official API (needs an API key), but only periodic aggregate datasets — not a live notice feed. Not useful for same-day detection; skipped by the checker.

sources.name: TEMPLATE — a genuine official JSON API, if one is ever found
sources.notes: Not a real source — a worked example so a future genuine JSON API can be wired in without new code. 'fieldMap' below shows how run_pipeline.py's json_api adapter reads a response.
